newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AGA says restructuring costs hurt Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: AGA says restructuring costs hurt Q1 profit.

text.p: Swedish medical and industrial gas company AGA on Tuesday posted a fall in first quarter earnings and said profit was also hurt by restructuring costs of 105 million crowns.
"AGA's new group organization, based on three business areas, will be in place by the end of the first half of the year," the company said in an earnings statement.
All costs for the restructuring had been taken in the first quarter, AGA said, adding that the full effects of the programme would occur in 1998.
Before restructuring costs, profit after financial items dropped 21 percent to 414 million crowns and after restructuring costs, profit landed at 309 million crowns.

"Apart from the restructuring, this decrease is mainly due to the weaker economic climate in several countries in Europe as well as higher depreciation and interest expenses attributable to the extensive investment programme," AGA said.
Depreciation amounted to 397 million crowns, up from 327 million, and net financial items swung to a charge of 18 million from a credit of 60 million.
Sales rose six percent to 3.40 billion crowns in the first quarter from 3.22 billion in the corresponding quarter.

Foreign exchange fluctuations accounted for two percent of the increase and operations acquired in 1996 in the U.S., Puerto Rico and Ukraine contributed about four percentage points, the company said.
"Otherwise sales remained unchanged, which was to some extent due to the 1997 Easter holiday occuring in March instead of April," AGA said.
"Volumes of liquid gases, primarily for the process industry, as well as specialty gases, increased substantially, while the volume trend for cylinder gases was weak."
Operating profit fell seven percent to 432 million crowns, excluding restructuring costs with the operating margin falling to 12.7 percent from 14.4 percent.
Earnings per share fell to 0.81 crown from 1.52 with restructuring costs having a negative impact of 0.30 crown.
"The business climate remained favourable in the U.S. and improved in many countries in Latin America but was still weak in most parts of Europe," the company said.

"As in 1996, there was price pressure in several markets. AGA's operating income was also affected by rising depreciation as a result of the extensive investment programme and company acquisitions in 1996."
Operating profit fell at operations in Germany, Austria, Colombia and some other countries, it said.
But operating profit increased in subsidiaries in the U.S., Brazil and Mexico as well as in the Finnish company which reported a recovery after the decline in 1996, AGA said.
